priceNote: Q2 delivery report tomorrow (Jul 2) — stock pre-ran +8% this week to $420, now AT analyst avg PT $421
summary: Tesla reports Q2 2026 vehicle deliveries tomorrow (July 2) with a consensus of 406K vehicles. The stock has pre-run +8% this week to $420 — now essentially AT the analyst average price target of $421. With Hold consensus from 26 analysts and only +9% upside to the median $458 target, this is a hold-and-watch moment: a delivery beat >415K could pop 5–10%, but the upside story depends entirely on Cybercab robotaxi expansion and Optimus production confirmation in H2.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Delivery Report
catalysts.description: Consensus 406K vehicles. Beat bar >415K = +5–10% pop; miss <395K = -8–12% drop. Energy storage consensus 13.8 GWh (+36% QoQ). Stock pre-ran +8% into this report — sell-the-news risk if in-line.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: EPS est. $0.42; rev est. $24.58B. Key watch: auto gross margin recovery and energy storage contribution. Q1 beat but -3.56% on $5B capex raise — capex commentary will drive the reaction more than the headline.

catalysts.name: Optimus Gen 3 — Production Start
catalysts.description: Musk at 2026 Abundance Summit: 'final stages of completion — most advanced robot in world.' Production starts Summer 2026; high-volume 2027 ramp. Long-term: 2M units/year goal.

catalysts.name: Cybercab Robotaxi — City Expansion
catalysts.description: Austin full metro live (Jun 8). H1 2026 deadline for 5 more cities (Las Vegas, Tampa, Orlando, Miami, Phoenix) MISSED. Engineering tests still running Jun 30. 7 cities targeted in 2026.

catalysts.name: FSD EU Type Approval
catalysts.description: EU Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) held first formal review Jun 30. EU-wide FSD/Robotaxi type approval would unlock a major new market. H2 2026 timeline.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed at 3.50–3.75%; Warsh removed easing bias Jun 17. EV demand is interest-rate sensitive (auto loans) but Tesla's AI/robotics narrative partially offsets — priced more as a tech stock.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE 3.4% (3-yr high). EV input costs (lithium, steel) are inflation-exposed. Iran conflict = higher energy prices could accelerate EV adoption long-term but near-term hits consumer spending.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Higher rates hurt EV affordability at the consumer level. However, Tesla's FSD/Cybercab/Optimus narrative makes it a tech stock — FOMC risk is about multiple compression, not just auto demand.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — rate headwinds compress the AI premium multiple. Stock at analyst avg PT leaves little margin of safety for any macro or earnings disappointment.
